name: The Thousand-Year Oak of Sacrow
verified_sources: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkmale_in_Potsdam (reproduces the city's Naturdenkmal list: no. 15, girth 685 cm, coordinates, Flurstueck 118/14)
access: Free. Stands in the Schlosspark Sacrow, a public landscape park by the Havel (Lenne design); open in daylight.
transport: By bus from central Potsdam to Sacrow, then on foot through the Schlosspark Sacrow to the oak.
verify_notes: Register only (official Potsdam Naturdenkmal list via de.wikipedia reproduction), one source for species and girth. Girth 685 cm is the thickest of the Potsdam oak monuments, from the register's Umfang column, no measurement date given. The name '1000-jaehrige Eiche' is the register's own designation, NOT a measured age: do not state 1000 years as fact, say 'known as the thousand-year oak'. No age field in the register. Commons has its own category 'Tausendjaehrige Eiche (Sacrow)' and photographs (file 1000-jaehrige Eiche in Sacrow, 1.jpg), so a photograph is in reach. Alive: iNaturalist observation 2025-06-29 at the coordinate (RECENT per lifecheck; proves something photographed there, not the trunk). Note the register's neighbouring Sacrow oaks nos. 13 and 14 (600 and 575 cm, Krampnitzer Strasse) have swapped Commons file labels (ND 13/ND 14), so identity of those two is ambiguous; left as leads.
story:
Potsdam's register calls this the thousand-year oak, and nobody has ever counted the thousand years. The name is the city's own designation for natural monument number 15, and it is a title rather than a date: the same register gives the tree a girth and a coordinate and leaves the age field out entirely.

The girth is the part that holds. At 685 centimetres round, close to seven metres of trunk, it is the thickest oak on Potsdam's whole list of natural monuments. Two more protected oaks stand a short walk away along the Krampnitzer Strasse, at 600 and 575 centimetres, and this one still outweighs them both. A pedunculate oak of that size is old by any reckoning. How old is a question a tape measure alone cannot settle, and the register does not try.

It stands in the Schlosspark Sacrow, the landscape park on the Havel shore laid out to a design by Lenné, open to walk in daylight and free. Someone photographed the spot in June 2025, which is the most recent sign of life on record, though the register does not say when its girth was taken.

So the honest version is this: Potsdam's thickest protected oak, wearing a name it may or may not have earned. If you know when it was last measured, or have a better idea of its age, tell us.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the trunk, 6.85 metres round, thicker than the two protected oaks a short walk away on the Krampnitzer Strasse. It stands in the Schlosspark Sacrow, by the Havel.

name: The Columnar Oaks of Bassinplatz
access: Free. A public city square in central Potsdam, open at all times.
transport: In central Potsdam, a short walk from the Brandenburger Tor.
verify_notes: FOLDED twin: register nos. 31 (52.401872, 13.062176, girth 600 cm) and 32 (52.40203, 13.06268, girth 395 cm) both on Flurstueck 692, about 40 m apart; shown as one stop, pin on no. 31. Register only, one source. Both are fastigiate (columnar) oaks, a cultivar, which is the point of them: an upright form of the English oak on a square. 600 cm girth is large for a fastigiate cultivar, which is a plain register figure, unverified by us (a girth like this on a columnar form is unusual; flagged in case it is a multi-stem measurement). No age in register; do not derive one. Alive: two iNaturalist observations dated 2026-06-18 at the two coordinates (RECENT). Photographs in reach on Commons (files named Naturdenkmal Nr. 31 / Nr. 32 Saeulen-Eiche auf dem Bassinplatz).
story:
Most oaks spread. These two go straight up. The pair on Bassinplatz are fastigiate oaks, a columnar form of the ordinary pedunculate oak that holds its branches close to the trunk and grows like a flame rather than a dome. Potsdam protects both as natural monuments, numbers 31 and 32, standing about forty metres apart on the same square.

The surprise is in the register's tape measure. It gives the larger one 600 centimetres round, six metres of trunk, which is a girth you expect from a broad veteran in open parkland and not from a cultivar bred to stay narrow. The second comes in at a more ordinary 395. We have not been able to check the bigger figure, and a number that size on a columnar tree could be a measurement taken around more than one stem, so read it as the register's word until somebody confirms it.

What is not in doubt is that both are standing: each was photographed in June 2026. The register gives neither of them an age, and nothing else we have found does either.

They make an odd sight in a city square, two green columns where you would expect a spreading crown, and they are among the easiest protected trees in Potsdam to reach, on open public ground in the centre. If you know how old they are, or have run a tape around the big one yourself, tell us.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise them by their shape: two narrow, upright oaks where you would expect broad crowns. They stand on Bassinplatz about 40 metres apart; the pin marks the thicker one, 6 metres round.

access: Free. On the public Weberplatz square beside the church; open at all times.

verify_notes: Register only, one source, flagged. Alive check weak: lifecheck returned OLD (2011) within the radius, and that Commons photo is of the square, not necessarily this trunk; no recent dated confirmation found, so the page should ask readers to confirm it still stands. The register's own place text 'an der Kirche vor der Sakristei' places it by the church, which is a clear recognition line. story:
Potsdam's register places this lime with unusual precision: by the church, in front of the sacristy. Most entries give a street. This one tells you which door to stand at.

It is a small-leaved lime, natural monument number 53, which the register measures at 380 centimetres round, close to four metres of trunk on a city square in Babelsberg. The register gives it no age, and we have found nobody who has dated it, so this page does not guess.

Weberplatz holds a second protected tree about seventy metres away, a white mulberry of nearly the same girth at the corner of the Lutherstrasse, and it is worth a look on the way past.

Here is the gap we will not paper over. The most recent photograph we can find of this spot dates from 2011, and it shows the square rather than this trunk. The lime is still on the register, but we cannot show you dated proof that it stands today, and a register is a list of what was protected rather than a report on what survived.

So this is a tree to check as much as to collect. If you pass the church on Weberplatz, look in front of the sacristy, and tell us whether the lime is still there. In early summer, if it is, you will smell it before you see it.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by where it stands: directly in front of the sacristy of the church on Weberplatz, a lime 3.8 metres round. The square's other protected tree, a white mulberry, is 70 metres away at the Lutherstrasse corner.

best_time.label: late June into July, when the lime flowers and the scent carries across the square

location.address: Schiffbauergasse cultural site, Berliner Strasse 28, 14467 Potsdam

access: Free. Stands on the grounds of the Schiffbauergasse cultural quarter on the Tiefer See, which is open to the public (theatre, restaurants, lakeside walk); not checked against opening times of individual venues.

Alive check weak: lifecheck returned OLD (2009) and the matched Commons file is a view of the Tiefer See, not clearly this trunk, so recent proof of life is missing and the page should ask readers. Commons has a dedicated photograph (Naturdenkmal Nr 29 Stiel-Eiche auf dem Gelaende der Schiffbauergasse.jpg), so a photograph is in reach. story:
This oak has a theatre for a neighbour. It stands on the grounds of the Schiffbauergasse, Potsdam's cultural quarter on the shore of the Tiefer See, where the evening crowd comes for a play, a meal or the lakeside walk and can easily walk straight past a protected tree.

The register lists it as natural monument number 29, a pedunculate oak measured at 480 centimetres round. Nearly five metres of trunk puts it among the larger oaks the city protects, though well behind the thousand-year oak at Sacrow, which tapes 685. Nobody has recorded its age, and we have found no source that tries, so this page leaves the number empty rather than inventing one.

There is a second gap, and it matters more. The most recent dated picture we can find from this spot is from 2009, and it looks out over the lake rather than at the trunk. The oak is still on the register, but we cannot show you recent proof that it stands, and a register records what was protected, not what survived.

The grounds themselves are open to the public, so checking is easy: come for the lake or the theatre and look for the big oak on the way. If it is there, or if it is not, tell us. Either answer makes this page better.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the large oak on the Schiffbauergasse grounds by the Tiefer See, 4.8 metres round; the pin is the register's own point for this tree.

name: The Oaks of the Jungfernsee

location.address: Bertinistrasse, on the shore of the Jungfernsee, 14467 Potsdam

verified_sources: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkmale_in_Potsdam (no. 19, three oaks, girths 460, 515 and 590 cm, three coordinates)
access: Free to see from the Bertinistrasse and the shore path by the lake. The register places the three oaks on three separate land parcels, and whether any of them stands inside a fenced private plot has not been confirmed, so look from the street and the path.
transport: On the Jungfernsee shore north of the centre, along the Bertinistrasse.
verify_notes: Register only, one source. Three oaks, register points 52.429927,13.064992 / 52.429316,13.064753 / 52.428601,13.064674, spread over about 150 m along the shore: a trio read as one stop, not a single trunk. Girths 460, 515 and 590 cm, but the register does not say which point carries which girth, so the thickest cannot be pinned individually: pin is the northernmost point and precision is approximate for that reason. Alive: Commons photograph dated 2025-04-27 of the trio (RECENT). A photograph is in reach on Commons (Stiel-Eichen am Jungfernsee).
story:
Three oaks share one entry in Potsdam's register, and the register will not tell you which is which. Natural monument number 19 is a trio of pedunculate oaks strung along about 150 metres of the Jungfernsee shore by the Bertinistrasse, with girths of 460, 515 and 590 centimetres and three separate coordinates. What it does not record is which girth belongs to which point.

That turns the biggest of them, close to six metres round, into a small puzzle for whoever comes to look: it is one of these three, and a tape measure is the only way to settle which. Our pin sits on the northernmost of the register's three points, which is why this page marks it as approximate. Walk the shore and all three stand along the same stretch.

They were photographed together in April 2025, so all three were standing then. Nobody has recorded an age for any of them, and we have not found a source that guesses.

One more honest note. The register puts them on three different land parcels, and we have not confirmed whether any of them stands behind a private fence. Look from the street and the shore path, and leave the gardens alone. If you can tell us which of the three is the 590, or roughly how old they are, please do.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise them as three large oaks spread over about 150 metres of the Jungfernsee shore by the Bertinistrasse. The pin is the northernmost; the thickest, 5.9 metres round, is one of the three.

story:
Four and a half metres of sessile oak stand beside a dirt track, at the edge of an allotment colony in the Templiner Vorstadt. Potsdam lists it as natural monument number 39 and gives two reasons for protecting it: its scientific value, and its character and beauty.

The girth is the number everyone agrees on. The city's own page, the German Wikipedia list of Potsdam's natural monuments and the OpenStreetMap entry all give 450 centimetres. The city's page adds that the species can reach six metres round, which puts this one three quarters of the way there.

It is also easy to find. The unpaved southern stretch of the Paetowstrasse runs past the Kolonie Sternschanze allotments, and the oak stands about five metres off the track. A photograph from January 2021 and a map entry from the same year put it on exactly the same spot, which is why the pin here sits on the tree. The coordinate in the public list of Potsdam's monuments is about 26 metres out.

The thin part is the recent past. That 2021 photograph is the latest sighting we have, and nobody has published an age for the tree. If you walk past, tell us it still stands, and if you know how old it is, tell us that too.

The Hauptbahnhof is about 20 minutes away on foot. Some 80 to 100 metres south-west, the register lists a group of Turkey oaks as monument number 40.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the trunk, 4.5 metres round. It stands about five metres off the unpaved southern end of the Paetowstrasse, beside the Kolonie Sternschanze allotments.

story:
A German tree archive says one of the trunks here is really two oaks grown into one. Potsdam protects three pedunculate oaks behind the last houses of the Weinmeisterweg in Sacrow as natural monument number 12, and gives them girths of 470, 560 and 650 centimetres. The Ostdeutsches Baumarchiv, a private record of old trees, counted them differently on its 2021 visit: one oak at 589 centimetres, and a twin, fused at the base and grown together above chest height, which it could only tape as a single trunk of 673.

The two sets of numbers do not quite meet. The twin comes out larger than the register's biggest oak, which fits a tree that kept growing after the city measured it, or a tape held at another height. The register does not say when it measured, so both figures stand here and neither is corrected into the other.

The city protects them for science, rarity, distinctiveness and beauty. It gives no age, and nobody we have found has dated them.

Getting there means passing the last houses at the forest edge. The map shows a bollard on the way in that lets walkers through, with private gates and a private service road close by. Keep to the public way and out of the gardens.

The latest sighting we know of is that 2021 visit. If you go, tell us they still stand. The thousand-year oak in the Schlosspark is about 500 metres away.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise them as three big oaks within about 25 metres of each other, behind the last houses at the forest edge west of the Weinmeisterweg. The pin is on the thickest, 6.5 metres round.

story:
One tree archive has come back to this roadside oak seven times since 2000, most recently in 2021. Natural monument number 14 is a pedunculate oak on the Krampnitzer Strasse in Sacrow, roughly opposite the turning into the Fährstrasse, and nothing about it is behind a gate: you see it from the street.

Potsdam's register gives it 575 centimetres round. The Ostdeutsches Baumarchiv, a private record of old trees in eastern Germany, taped 596 in 2021. The gap fits a tree that grew after the city measured it, or a tape held at another height, so both numbers are kept.

The archive also lists the paperwork behind it: an ordinance for the old Osthavelland district in 1949, and the Potsdam ordinance of 2005 that protects it today. Neither the register nor the archive gives it an age, and we have not found anyone who has.

One warning about the pin. The register's coordinate sits by the Fährstrasse junction, which matches both written descriptions, but an online map puts the tree about 55 metres further east, and we have not settled which is right. So our pin is approximate. Go by the junction instead: the archive puts the oak about 20 metres north of it, just before the Fährstrasse comes in.

The thousand-year oak in the Schlosspark is about 300 metres to the west. If you know this tree's age, tell us.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the big oak at the roadside of the Krampnitzer Strasse, about 20 metres north of where the Fährstrasse joins it. The pin is approximate, so trust the junction over the dot.

story:
This natural monument is a street tree. Potsdam protected it on 21 November 2005 as number 33, and the city's own page places it with the precision of a delivery note: in the street Am Kanal, opposite number 71, at the roadside.

It is a London plane, the hybrid that lines city streets across Europe, and the city's page marks it as a foreign species. That is part of what makes it odd company. Every other Potsdam tree on this page is an oak or a lime, standing in a park, on a square or at a forest edge. This one stands at a kerb in the middle of town, and made the list anyway.

The city's page gives its girth as 423 centimetres; the German Wikipedia list of Potsdam's monuments says 426. Three centimetres is a small enough gap to be a tape held a little higher or lower, and both figures are on record. Either way, more than four metres of trunk at the edge of a road.

Nobody has published an age for it, so this page gives none. The most recent photographs we know of were uploaded in December 2020, which is thin proof for today. If you walk past, tell us it still stands.

The columnar oaks on Bassinplatz are about 550 metres away, which makes the two an easy pair for a walk through the centre.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the plane tree at the roadside of Am Kanal, directly across from number 71, its trunk more than 4.2 metres round.

access: Free. Per Ostdeutsches Baumarchiv ('Zugang: Frei zugaenglich', visited 2009 to 2023) the oak stands on open lawn with a playground between new housing and a school on the former barracks site; the site was redeveloped, so the housing estate's paths are the way in. Not checked against OSM access tags or a city source.
transport: Potsdam Nord, former Rote Kaserne off Fritz-von-der-Lancken-Strasse near the Nedlitzer Strasse (stops not checked).
verify_notes: Register: city page (fetched 2026-10-20, Flur 1 Flurstueck 293, girth 505 cm, 'im noerdlichen Teil der ehemaligen Roten Kaserne', Fritz-von-der-Lancken-Strasse); designation 2005-11-21 per Wikidata; de.wikipedia list coordinate 52.427162,13.056581. Ostdeutsches Baumarchiv (private archive, not an authority): solitary Stiel-Eiche 'gegenueber der Schule', visited 2009, 2010, 2014, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022 and twice in 2023, girth 550 cm at 1.3 m in 2023, photo 2021, GPS 52.427162,13.056471. Two independent coordinates 10 m apart on a solitary crown: pin set between them, confirmed. story:
Potsdam lists this oak as natural monument number 10. The tree archive that has visited it nine times since 2009 says it is not a natural monument at all.

The disagreement may be paperwork rather than anything about the tree. The city's own list carries it, and Wikidata records its designation in November 2005; the archive's entry began as a find in 2009 and may simply never have caught up. We go by the city's list, and we say that is where the protection comes from.

It stands in the northern part of the former Rote Kaserne, the Red Barracks, a site since rebuilt as new housing and a school. The archive describes a solitary oak on open lawn with a playground, across from the school, and the paths of the housing estate are the way in.

The tape gives two answers. The city's page says 505 centimetres round; the archive measured 550 at chest height in 2023. That fits a tree that grew after the city's measurement, or a tape held at another height, and both figures are kept. The archive also records that the crown has been cut back several times in recent years.

Nobody has published a reliable age for it, so this page gives none. If you know how old it is, tell us. The last visit we know of was in 2023.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the lone big oak on the open lawn with the playground, across from the school in the northern part of the former Rote Kaserne. Its trunk is about 5.5 metres round.

story:
Potsdam numbers its natural monuments, and number one is a linden in Fahrland that has been cut back on purpose, again and again.

The city's register calls it a Kopfbaum, a pollard: a tree whose crown is cut back at regular intervals and left to grow a fresh head of shoots. Pollarding is how people took wood from a tree without felling it, and the city notes that old pollards like this one become homes for birds and insects. The trunk under that cropped head measures 3.83 metres round.

It stands at the roadside of An der Jubelitz, across the street from the mill, in Fahrland, a village district on Potsdam's northern edge about nine kilometres from the centre. One published version of the register list gives its address as Ketzinerstrasse 37 instead. The city's own page and the mapped tree both put it on An der Jubelitz, opposite the mill, and that is where our pin sits.

Two things nobody has written down. The register names it only as Tilia, a linden, without saying which kind. And no source gives its age, so we will not guess one. If you can tell the species from its leaves, or know how long it has stood by the mill, tell us.

It is a street tree: no gate, no ticket, and you can look at it at any hour.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by its pollarded crown, cut back at regular intervals, above a trunk 3.83 metres round. It stands at the roadside of An der Jubelitz, across the street from the mill.

Species only to genus in the register (Tilia spec.). The city page says the linden was trained as a pollard (Kopfbaum), cut back at regular intervals; pollards are a wood-harvest form that keeps the tree without felling it, and old pollards are habitat for birds and insects (the page's own wording). story:
Potsdam protects this oak for three reasons at once: its beauty, its place in local history, and its scientific value. It stands in an ordinary city street, between house numbers 1 and 3 on Babelsberger Strasse.

The city lists it as natural monument number 36, a pedunculate oak with a trunk 3.67 metres round. That is a serious waistline for a street tree, and it is the one hard measurement anyone has published.

The register names local history as a reason without saying which history it means, and we have found no source that does, so we will not guess at it. The same goes for its age: no source gives one, and a girth alone is not enough for us to put a number on it. If you know the story of this oak, or roughly when it went in, tell us. It would be the first time either was written down.

What we can vouch for is the spot. The city's register and the mapped tree agree to within about eleven metres, a photograph of it as a natural monument sits in the public Wikimedia Commons archive, and an iNaturalist sighting was logged here in 2023.

It is a street tree, free to see from the pavement at any hour, and about fifteen minutes on foot from Potsdam Hauptbahnhof.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by its trunk, 3.67 metres round, a pedunculate oak in a street of houses. It stands in Babelsberger Strasse, between house numbers 1 and 3.

story:
Potsdam protects these three limes for their rarity, their character and their place in local history, and counts them as one natural monument: number 8 on the city's register.

They are small-leaved limes, measured at 4.70, 4.10 and 3.90 metres round, and they stand within about twelve metres of one another. The register places them at the roadside of the Mühlendamm and in the churchyard of Nattwerder's village church. It does not say which trunk stands where, so we treat the three as one stop and have put the pin on the largest.

Nattwerder is a hamlet by the Havel, about twelve kilometres west of central Potsdam. The register does not spell out the local history it has in mind, and no source we found gives the trees an age. We will not invent either. If you know how old they are, or why the village values them, tell us.

We should also be plain about how recently anyone has looked. The city still lists all three, but we have found no recent photograph or sighting of them. If you go, a picture of the three trunks would be the first we could show here.

You can see them from the village street. We have not checked when the churchyard gate is open. Small-leaved limes flower late, in July, and that is the month to come, when the blossom scents the air around the church.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise them as three small-leaved limes within about twelve metres of each other, the largest 4.70 metres round. They stand by the Mühlendamm and in the churchyard of Nattwerder's village church.

best_time.label: July, when the three limes flower late and scent the churchyard
